reason: 'It asked for a number, then checked every number from 2 up to the one you entered... She typed 7 and got "prime," also right.' A loop that tests the input itself as a divisor (the bug the story blames for 2) would also report 7 as not prime, so the described debugging trace is wrong.

'a blue logo with a bowl shape... That's the network... Feeding America.' Feeding America's logo is orange and green, not blue (logotyp.us; food-bank brand guidelines: Pantone 144 orange, Pantone 371 green).

'It came from the direction of the pond... the ground sloped downhill toward the water... the slope would make it drift faster and farther.' A wind blowing from the pond pushes the frame away from the pond, uphill, so the slope would slow it, not speed it; the reasoning the plot rewards is backwards.

'She rinsed the chicken, patted it dry' is shown as a normal step in a food-safety story. USDA FSIS advises not washing raw poultry because rinsing splashes bacteria onto the sink and nearby food, including salad.

'If he sneezed on the taco bar on Friday [day five], that would be fine' and the closing 'three days of being a walking sneeze... day five' present people as no longer contagious after day three. CDC (How Flu Spreads) says flu can spread for up to 5-7 days after becoming sick.

'the b had probably once done its job before the vowels moved on without it. It wasn't a guess anymore.' The b in 'subtle' was never pronounced in English; it was added in a Latin-style respelling (from Old French sotil) and has nothing to do with the Great Vowel Shift (Etymonline, 'subtle').
'nine bean plants in paper cups... Three said Fertilizer A, three said Fertilizer B, and one just said Water.' 3 + 3 + 1 = 7, not nine.

'The compound payments did. Three dollars twelve. Three dollars ninety.' At the story's 5% rate ($2.50 on $50), yearly compound interest is $2.50, $2.63, $2.76, $2.89 and $3.04; it never reaches $3.12 or $3.90 within five years.
'eleven, thirteen, twelve, fourteen, ten, twelve, eleven, fifteen, twelve, thirteen... Four of them were twelve.' Only three of the listed answers are twelve (the median is still 12).
